decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'In the "Save a link" box at the top, paste any web address... and press Save.' R3 client: 'Saving from a single web-address box feels right and pleasantly quick.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Single-URL save box conforms to REF-BM-01; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'since I only asked you for a web address, I guessed a title from the address itself... Later we could instead pull the page's real title automatically.' R3 client: 'I'd want the app to fetch the page's real title automatically and let me change it.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented title was guessed from the URL, diverging from REF-BM-02 auto-collection; client supplies the reference-conforming auto-fetch plus editability (REF-BM-03). Delivered R4.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'I chose to display a title, the web address, and the time you saved it... is something missing or unnecessary?' R3 client: 'At a glance, I'd prefer the real title, a short description, tags, and the site icon. The address and saved time can be secondary.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented list item showed only title/url/time, diverging from REF-BM-07 (title, description, tags, favicon). Client replaces it with the reference-conforming set.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker described items only 'drop into your library... showing the site, a title, and when you saved it' (no open behaviour). R3 client: 'Most importantly, clicking the saved item should open the original page; otherwise I can't actually revisit the bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Open-original was absent from the presented scope; client requests the missing related reference requirement REF-BM-08. Delivered R4.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: card fills with 'a real title, a short description, the site icon, and — smaller, underneath — the site and saved time' (no preview image). R4 client: 'Yes, this matches what I had in mind.' Preview image never mentioned by anyone through R22.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-02 also requires a preview image; the auto-collected set omits it throughout. The omission passed with approval and no explicit expression of the difference — unexpressed divergence (separable aspect from the auto-title correction in R3).

decisions.evidence: R5 maker offered Version A (free type & enter, no autocomplete), B (pick from existing tags + create new), C (details panel). R5 client: 'Version B feels best for everyday use because seeing existing tags will help me stay consistent, while still letting me create a new one when needed.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Offered alternatives differ in fulfilling REF-BM-10 (A has no autocomplete of existing tags; B does). Client selects the reference-conforming alternative; decision marked diverged=true per select rule.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker put a plain highlighted-strip note on the card ('My assumption is notes are usually short reminders'), no markdown. R6 client: 'I'll sometimes want a longer write-up with simple Markdown formatting. I'd show a short preview... then let me expand or open the full rendered note.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented note lacked markdown rendering, diverging from REF-BM-23; client supplies reference-conforming markdown-with-render behaviour. Delivered R7.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presented only free-text multi-field live search. R8 client: 'I'd also like a precise way to search when needed: #tag for a specific tag...'
decisions.note: Prototype review. #tag syntax absent from presented search; client requests the missing reference requirement REF-BM-14. Delivered R9.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker: no phrase matching presented. R8 client: '...quoted phrases for an exact match...'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Exact-phrase search absent; client requests missing reference requirement REF-BM-16. Delivered R9.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker: only 'all words must match' presented. R8 client: '...and AND, OR, NOT, plus parentheses for combinations.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Boolean operators/parentheses absent; client requests missing reference requirement REF-BM-15. Delivered R9.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker did not state case handling. R8 client: 'Search should ignore capitalization.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitivity not in presented scope; client requests reference requirement REF-BM-13. Delivered R9.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'the operators must be typed in capitals (AND, not and)... would you rather lowercase and/or/not also act as operators?' R9 client: 'Requiring capitalized AND, OR, and NOT works for me and makes lowercase words behave predictably.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Reference REF-BM-15's rule is that operators must be *quoted* to be literal (its example uses lowercase 'or' as an operator). The capitals-only mechanism diverges; the reference-conforming offered alternative was lowercase-also-operators. Client explicitly states the specific behaviour and its consequence and accepts the departure rather than aligning — accepted divergence, distinct aspect from the R8 boolean-search extend.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker presented opt-in reading-list flag, separate Reading-list view, mark-read removes but keeps in Library. R10 client: 'The opt-in model fits... marking one as read should remove it from the Reading list without deleting it.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reading-list behaviour conforms to REF-BM-17/18/19; the opt-in vs inbox-first choice does not fail a reference item (reference marks 'read later' as a user action).

decisions.evidence: R11 maker: archive tab; archived leave Library+Reading list, recoverable via Restore; search scoped to current tab. R11 client: 'Archived links should disappear from both the Library and Reading list, remain fully recoverable, and only appear in searches while I'm viewing the Archive.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforms to REF-BM-26/27/28 and the archive edge-case rules; client's confirmation restates conforming behaviour.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker: 'The preserved copy captures the page's readable content... rather than a pixel-perfect photograph' — presented uniformly for every link. R12 client: 'For a link that points directly to a PDF, I'd want the original PDF preserved instead of converting it into a reader-style page.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented single readable-content copy for all links diverged from REF-BM-24's PDF rule; client supplies the reference-conforming PDF-as-original distinction. Delivered R13.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker declared 'that's the last of the capabilities from your original goal.' R13 client: 'I still need to... edit their address and description—not only the title.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Only title was editable (R4 rename); URL and description editing were missing, diverging from REF-BM-04. Client requests the missing edit fields. Delivered R14.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker declared the capability set complete. R13 client: 'I still need to delete bookmarks...'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Delete was absent from the presented app, diverging from REF-BM-05; client requests it. Delivered R14.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker declared completeness. R13 client: '...and avoid creating a duplicate when I save an address that's already in my library.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Duplicate-prevention absent, diverging from REF-BM-06; client requests convergence-to-edit-existing behaviour. Delivered R14.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker: 'Delete is permanent and needs confirmation... would you prefer deleted items go to a recoverable trash first?' R14 client: 'Permanent deletion with a clear confirmation is enough; I don't need a separate trash area.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Offered alternatives differ in fulfilling REF-BM-27 (a recoverable trash would contradict 'delete is permanent removal'). Client selects the reference-conforming permanent-delete option; decision marked diverged=true per select rule.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker described normalization (http/https, www, trailing slash, #section same; different query = different) with a 'Show it' jump to the existing card. R14 client: 'The duplicate rules also match my expectations, including treating different query strings as potentially different pages.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivered duplicate detection conforms to REF-BM-06 and its edge case; normalization details are functionally equivalent implementation choices confirmed by the client.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker: 'Editing the address keeps the existing saved copy, tags, and notes attached. Reasonable, or would changing the address mean it should be treated as a new page?' R14 client: 'When an address changes, keep my tags and note attached, but fetch the new page's details and capture a fresh saved copy. Keeping the old page copy under the new address would be misleading.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented behaviour retained the old snapshot/details under a changed URL, diverging from REF-BM-24 (snapshot of the bookmarked page) and REF-BM-02 (collect the target page's details); client supplies the reference-conforming refetch/re-snapshot. Delivered R15.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker's 'big' demo tested one oversized bookmark only. R16 client: 'With hundreds of links, I'd need sorting—such as by date added or title...'
decisions.note: Prototype review (boundary). Sorting was absent from the presented app, diverging from REF-BM-22; client requests it. Delivered R17.

decisions.evidence: R16 client: '...and multi-select actions for tagging, marking read or unread, archiving, and deleting.'
decisions.note: Prototype review (boundary). Multi-select bulk actions were absent, diverging from REF-BM-20; client requests them. Delivered R17.

decisions.evidence: R16 client: 'It should also be possible to apply an action to every bookmark matching the current search, tag, or tab, not accidentally to the entire library.'
decisions.note: Prototype review (boundary). Filtered-scope bulk application was absent, diverging from REF-BM-21; client requests the scoped whole-collection action. Delivered R17.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker: 'Newest first, Oldest first, and Title A–Z... is there another ordering you'd reach for?' R17 client: 'Newest, Oldest, and Title A–Z cover the sorting I'd use most often.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Delivered sort options conform to REF-BM-22 ('date added, title, etc.'); client confirms adequacy (functionally equivalent to reference).

decisions.evidence: R17 maker: explicit selection with 'Select all N in results for...' stating count and scope. R17 client: 'The explicit selection count and named scope give me enough confidence.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Delivered scoped bulk selection conforms to REF-BM-21.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker's bulk actions offered '＋ Add tag' but no remove. R17 client: 'bulk tagging should let me remove a tag from the selected links as well as add one.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Delivered bulk tagging was add-only, diverging from REF-BM-20's explicit 'add/remove tags'; client requests the missing remove-tag half. Delivered R18. Separate stage/aspect from the R16 REF-BM-20 request.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker: '－ Remove tag... removing one strips it from all selected links.' R18 client: 'Yes, that completes the bulk-tagging flow I need.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Delivered bulk remove-tag now conforms to REF-BM-20.
